principle_text: When the persuadee expresses a nuanced or complex view, avoid giving vague or overly general responses that do not advance the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee expresses a strong belief in overall peace despite some issues, avoid introducing conflicting information without connecting it to their values or concerns.
When the persuadee redirects concern to a different issue, avoid focusing solely on one aspect without addressing their specific concerns to maintain engagement and relevance.
When the persuadee shifts focus to a different global issue, avoid simply acknowledging without linking back to the charitable cause or donation appeal.
When the persuadee expresses specific concerns about an issue, avoid vague or non-informative responses that do not acknowledge or build on their expressed concerns.
When the persuadee expresses concern about global issues but does not connect to the charitable cause, avoid generic acknowledgments that do not guide the conversation toward the donation goal.

When the persuadee expresses agreement with general positive statements but does not show donation intent, avoid making broad statements that do not link to specific charitable actions or donation appeals.

When the persuadee is engaged in a positive, forward-looking discussion, avoid abruptly shifting to a direct donation request without first connecting the request to the ongoing conversation or the charity's mission.
When a persuadee declines to donate, avoid ending the conversation without attempting to re-engage or reinforce the donation appeal to maintain persuasion momentum.
When the persuadee shows initial indifference, you should evoke emotional responses by sharing impactful, specific stories that highlight the severity of the issue to increase empathy and concern.
